questions.stem: A service fires ten calls together, all sharing a 30,000-token prefix, against a cold cache. What does the module predict?

options.text: One writes and nine read, since all ten share the same hash and the same prefix
options.says: Ruled out because the entry "only becomes available after the first response begins", so the others have nothing to read.

options.text: Each one writes, since the entry appears only once a first reply starts
options.says: The page says a cache entry "only becomes available after the first response begins", so all ten write.

options.text: All read, since the entry is created the moment a request arrives
options.says: Ruled out because the same sentence says it is available only "after the first response begins".

options.text: One writes and nine fail, since an entry allows a single writer
options.says: Ruled out because the advice is "wait for the first response before sending subsequent requests", not that extra requests fail.

questions.stem: A prefix is sent twice within five minutes on a model that reads at 0.1 times the base price. How does the spend on the pair compare with two ordinary sends?

options.says: A five-minute write at 1.25 plus a read at 0.1 gives 1.35 against 2, about two thirds.
Ruled out because the first send alone costs more than that: "5-minute cache write tokens are 1.25 times the base input tokens price".
Ruled out because that figure is the one-hour case, from "1-hour cache write tokens are 2 times the base input tokens price".

options.text: About the same as two plain sends
options.says: Ruled out because the second send is a read: "Cache read tokens are 0.1 times the base input tokens price".

origin.section: The price of a write and a read

questions.stem: A request marks the system block with a five-minute breakpoint and the final message with a one-hour breakpoint. What does the module say?

options.text: It violates the ordering rule, since the longer entry has to come first
options.says: The page says "Cache entries with longer TTL must appear before shorter TTLs".

options.text: It is accepted, with both entries billed at one common rate
options.says: Ruled out because the writes are billed differently: "1-hour cache write tokens are 2 times the base input tokens price".

options.text: It is accepted, with only the short entry written
options.says: Ruled out because "The usage object then splits the writes" by lifetime, so both can be written.

options.text: It violates a one-TTL rule, since a request carries one lifetime
options.says: Ruled out because "You can use both 1-hour and 5-minute cache controls in the same request" when ordered correctly.

questions.stem: A 600-token system prompt is marked on a model whose minimum is 512, and usage shows a write on every call and no reads. The prompt begins with the clock reading. What should the team do?

options.text: Pad the prompt so it clears the floor by a wider margin and stays well above it
options.says: Ruled out because padding only helps a prefix that falls short, since "A prefix shorter than the model's minimum is not cached", and writes on every call show that this prompt is cached and is not short.

options.text: Raise the TTL to an hour so the entry survives between uses and keeps being read
options.says: Ruled out because "Changes at each level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels", whatever the TTL.

options.text: Shift that line to the end and set the boundary where unchanging text stops
options.says: The planner puts "a volatile block moves to the very end of the request", after the last breakpoint.

options.text: Switch to a larger number of explicit markers so more segments are cached separately
options.says: Ruled out because "You can define up to 4 cache breakpoints", yet an earlier changing block still changes the hash.

origin.section: The practice: order a request for cache hits
